physicalNotes: Radius: half the shadow diameter of a non-spinning black hole of the angular gravitational radius the EHT measured from its 2017 images, theta_g = GM/(D c^2) = 3.8 +/- 0.4 microarcseconds (EHT Collaboration 2019, ApJL 875, L1, M87 Paper I, Table 1, from Paper VI): d_sh = 6 sqrt(3) theta_g (EHT Collaboration 2022, Sgr A* Paper VI, arXiv:2311.09484, Section 3) = 39.49 microarcseconds; a spinning black hole's shadow is up to 7.5% smaller (same section). At the distance 16.8 Mpc (Paper I, Table 1): 19.745e-6 x 16.8e6 au = 331.72 au = 49,624,960,315 km at 149,597,870.7 km per au. It is the size of the dark region an observer sees, not an event horizon. GM from the mass (6.5 +/- 0.7) x 10^9 solar masses (Paper I, Table 1) times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2.

sources.position: SIMBAD M 87 (ICRS; coordinate reference 2020A&A...644A.159C, Charlot et al. 2020, ICRF3): https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=M+87
sources.distance: EHT Collaboration (2019, ApJL 875, L1; arXiv:1906.11238), M87 Paper I, Table 1: D = 16.8 +/- 0.8 Mpc, rederived from likelihood distributions in Paper VI.
sources.properMotion: Zero: M87 is an ICRF3 radio source (Charlot et al. 2020, A&A 644, A159), and the ICRF3 frame is defined by sources without proper motion. SIMBAD's -8.029, 10.734 mas/yr is an optical measurement of the galaxy's nucleus, far above any motion a galaxy 16.8 Mpc away can show.
sources.radialVelocity: SIMBAD M 87: 1256.48 km/s, from Abazajian et al. (2009, ApJS 182, 543; SDSS DR7), the redshift SIMBAD adopts.
